chunk_findings.detail: The handler decides whether a gate run is still open by testing `not g["outcome"]`. A `batch.gate_finished` event with a missing, null, or empty-string `outcome` is folded as `outcome=""` and `finished=ev.ts`, but the entry is still treated as open. Given a batch formed, a `batch.gate_started` for run `R`, then a `batch.gate_finished` for run `R` with no outcome, the folded gate entry remains open and can be matched by later finish events; a second finish for the same run/gate creates a duplicate gate entry instead of closing/updating the first. A finish event should close the run even when the outcome is unavailable; open/closed state should not depend on the truthiness of `outcome`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/batch.py:h_batch_gate_finished

chunk_findings.detail: `fan_out` obtains the gate definition only from the optional `gates` argument and never uses `cfg`. If the caller omits `gates` (the default), `gdef` is `None`, so both the human-gate guard and the evidence checks are skipped. For example, if `approve` is a human gate in `cfg`, a call like `fan_out(log, cfg, "b", gate="approve", outcome="passed", tree_sha="t")` records `gate.passed` for every member and a `batch.gate_finished` outcome, even though the docstring says a human gate must raise `ValueError`. chunk_findings.detail: `batch.dissolved` declares `text = ["reason"]`, so the reason is part of the event’s recorded evidence. chunk_findings.detail: The new started-run guard says it requires “run {run} of {gate} on tree {tree_sha}” to have been started, but the predicate only checks `g["run"] == run and not g.get("finished")`. It never compares the open gate’s `tree_sha` (nor its `gate` if run ids are not guaranteed globally unique). For example, after a batch is formed and `batch.gate_started` records run `R` for gate `ci` on tree `A`, a call such as `fan_out(log, cfg, "b", gate="ci", outcome="passed", tree_sha="B", run="R")` sees run `R` as open and records passed member outcomes plus a finished batch gate with evidence `tree_sha="B"`, even though no gate run was started on tree `B`. The validation should require the open run’s tree (and, where appropriate, gate) to match the requested outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/batchgate.py:141

chunk_findings.detail: The added test shows the duplicate-gate-run problem from the earlier finding is still present: after `BG.gate_started(..., run=R)`, a first `batch.gate_finished` for `R` with no outcome is folded, then a second `batch.gate_finished` for the same `R` with `outcome="passed"` is folded as a separate gate entry (`len(...gates) == 2`). That means one started run identifier now yields two folded gate entries, one with an empty outcome and one passed. A fold that is supposed to rebuild a gate run from its events should not turn the same `run` id into two runs; the second finish should update/ignore/reject the already-closed run. As written, any consumer that keys or matches gate state by `run`, or expects one outcome per started run, sees an ambiguous/duplicate outcome for `R`.
